findings.evidence: The active completion-lifecycle delta requires publication and Requirement lifecycle entrypoints to use the shared selector and fail explicitly for unsupported source combinations. In template/scripts/requirement_integration.py:814–820, publish_candidate checks only publish_mode and can return through _reconcile_exact_merged before reaching project_publish's selector. With platform_version=source and scm_provider=gitlab or harness_mode=project, _reconcile_exact_merged proceeds to sync main, reconcile child Project states, and reconcile the parent (lines 784–790). The directly callable template/scripts/requirement_terminal.py:47 reconcile_parent also never selects lifecycle mode before terminal Project reconciliation and Issue closure. Consequently these paths can report terminal delivery instead of rejecting the unsupported contract.
findings.summary: Shared Requirement publication and terminal reconciliation can complete under an unsupported source contract without invoking the lifecycle selector.
